evidence: Both surviving solutions build an adjacency list from the links; the statement explicitly says links total exactly n - 1 and that between any two outposts there is exactly one possible route. Their intended computation is therefore the union of the unique paths connecting the primary hubs.
affordance_in_statement: Furthermore, if all available comm-links were activated, between any two outposts there would be exactly one possible route of comm-links.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: the unique-route/tree structure is the core mathematical property that makes the task a linear-time subtree-sum problem. Replacing it with a general graph would change the task rather than merely remove wording.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats the input as a tree and constructs adjacency lists, enabling a traversal that selects exactly the edges in the minimal subtree spanning the hubs.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: the available comm-links connect all outposts such that there are exactly n - 1 possible comm-links in total

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the unique-path tree representation and an early return for the one-hub case; its adjacency construction is directly enabled by the tree guarantee.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: between any two outposts there would be exactly one possible route of comm-links

common_affordance: The available links form a connected tree, so the required network is simply the unique minimal subtree containing all primary hubs.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It repeatedly searches for and reconstructs paths between hubs, causing excessive repeated graph traversals and TLE instead of doing one tree traversal.
Its selected-edge logic does not correctly enforce that an edge belongs only when primary hubs occur on both sides of the edge, producing an incorrect total on branching cases.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat all survivors without changing the task: the tree/unique-route guarantee is an intrinsic structural floor. If changing the task is permitted, remove the unique-route guarantee and allow alternate routes, turning the problem into a general weighted-Steiner-subgraph problem.
